topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture with introductory framing on the importance and nomenclature challenges of studying the complement system.

topics.label: Foundations and core mechanism of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts, naming conventions, and central biochemical role of C3 activation in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms of the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways that trigger complement activation on target surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary downstream effector mechanisms by which activated complement eliminates pathogens and stimulates immunity.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host cells from complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic and acquired deficiencies in specific complement components result in distinct clinical disease presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and biomedical applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens evade complement destruction and how bacterial evasion factors are utilized in laboratory and therapeutic settings.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides closing framing, concluding the complement topic and previewing the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
